Audit-recommended target (never-attacked examples/occasion screen). leaks_ranked.why_real: The preview page is the peak-delight moment (creator watches the finished video, autoplay) yet produces ~0 review clicks despite real, recurring traffic (28-34 opens/window). Session replay confirms people REACH and ENGAGE the preview PAGE (e.g. 45s active, 13 clicks), which rules out the coarse 'never open the emailed video' reach failure. It does NOT, however, establish that arrivers scrolled past the autoplay video + the primary Send CTA + the <hr> divider to actually SEE the below-fold review ask - active-seconds as low as 7s (07-21 14:21, 07-20 02:59) are consistent with never reaching it. Almost all review clicks (11/11 this window) come from the single in-app thank-you screen.
leaks_ranked.size_of_prize: Direct feed to reviews (the objective) and a currently-WASTED high-intent moment, so downside is ~0 (cannot do worse than ~0 clicks). Prize is modest in absolute terms (a few reviews/fortnight) but compounds, is on the objective directly, and is the safest untried visible bet available.

biggest_leak: The biggest leak by headcount is the claim email gate, but I am deliberately NOT shipping there this cycle; I chose leak #3 (the ~0-converting preview-page review ask) for the visible experiment because it feeds reviews directly, is safe (downside ~0 on a currently-dead surface), is a genuinely untried mechanism, and it breaks four cycles of claim-page/instrumentation fixation. NOTE: I do NOT claim a verified cause here - the ask being generic is a code fact, but whether it is seen-and-ignored (H3) vs never-scrolled-into-view (H1b) is UNRESOLVED; the ship rests on the asymmetric-bet basis, not on a proven cause.

choice_reasoning.expected_value_to_reviews: The objective is reviews, and ~all reviews (11/11 this window) come from review-ask surfaces. The preview page is a second, better-timed ask (video just watched) to ~28 people/fortnight, of whom a meaningful (but not precisely known) share did NOT click review on the in-app screen - the ~61% in-app non-click figure is lag-truncated and overstates that un-converted pool, so treat it as a loose upper bound - currently yielding ~0. Even recovering a handful of clicks per fortnight is net-new honest reviews at ~zero risk, and it compounds. The claim gate, by contrast, is many probabilistic steps from a review per lost person; the warm-user step has higher per-person value but an unverifiable cause this cycle.
choice_reasoning.already_tried_here: Coverage map: 'Review ask: preview + share surfaces - 1 attempt. Reworked in June (non-destructive post-share highlight) -> still ~0 clicks.' That was ONE mechanism (a post-share pulse/scroll to draw the eye). One flat attempt does not retire the step; a different mechanism (motivational copy reframe at watch-time) is fair game and is what I propose.
choice_reasoning.what_history_suggests: Pattern across all changes: MECHANISM/motivation changes at warm, in-flow moments moved this funnel (2026-06-16 email-first + value-prop hero, +14pts into-app->video, held 3 weeks; making the in-app review ask the hero now produces almost all review clicks), while PRESENTATION reshuffles of a cold page did nothing (PR #8 claim-page layout, flat). Implication: bet on WHY-you-should copy at a high-intent moment (preview, post-watch), not on re-arranging a page. My change is a motivational reframe at the highest-delight moment - the kind that has worked here - so odds are better than a layout shuffle, though still unmeasurable at this traffic.
choice_reasoning.why_not_the_others: Claim gate (leak #1): fenced and unshippable this cycle - PR #8 layout redesign is spent ground, 'give the discount first' is owner-rejected, referencing the printed % is owner-rejected, and I found no NEW mechanism whose cause my evidence supports (replay shows a large share are low-intent instant bounces, not people repelled by the ask); it is also not freshly measurable (PostHog 403, page_viewed too new). Continuing to instrument it would be a fourth straight invisible cycle, explicitly disallowed. Warm-user step (leak #2): highest per-person value and audit-recommended, but the losing sub-step cannot be localized (in-app micro-steps undercounted, PostHog 403, replays sparse), so any fix would bet on an unverifiable cause - the exact mistake the last cycle was caught making. Preview (leak #3) is chosen not because its cause is verified (H3 vs H1b below-fold is unresolved) but because it is the only ranked leak addressable this cycle by a zero-downside, copy-only, reversible edit on a currently-dead (~0) surface - an asymmetric bet, not a cause-proven fix.

diagnosis.question: Why does the preview page - the moment the creator actually WATCHES their finished video - produce ~0 review clicks, when the (video-less, anticipation-only) in-app thank-you screen produces almost all of them?
hypotheses_considered: H1 They never reach/see the preview review ask (below the fold / never open the emailed video).
H2 Redundancy: they were already asked on the in-app thank-you screen minutes earlier and declined, so the moment is spent.

H3 The preview ask is generic and seller-oriented ('Made You Smile? / we would appreciate a review') and does not connect to the delight of the video they just watched or to their pride in making it; the page's gravity is 'send it' (primary CTA = Send My Gift Message).
H4 The whole surface is low-traffic noise not worth touching.
diagnosis.evidence_gathered: Supabase funnel-report both windows (review clicks by phase x role x source): this window 11/11 from in_app thankyou, 0 from preview; prior window 2 from preview_receiver of 34 opens. PostHog session_recordings API (HTTP 200): 6 in-window preview recordings show people reach and engage the PAGE (e.g. 07-21 16:14 active=45s clicks=13 keys=0; 07-21 14:21 active=7s clicks=6) but produce no review click - this contradicts only the COARSE reach failure 'never open the emailed video / never load preview' (H1a). It does NOT test whether they scrolled the below-divider ask into view (H1b), so replay cannot separate 'saw and ignored' (H3) from 'never saw below the fold' (H1b). In-app video_started->review_clicked = 39.3% (11/28) is a LAG-TRUNCATED same-window ratio (FUNNEL_CHANGELOG warns review clicks lag video creation by days via email reminders, so a frozen window undercounts them); it therefore OVERSTATES the un-converted share - '~61% did not click in-app' is a loose upper bound on the second-chance audience, not a firm floor, and only loosely bounds H2. Read the exact preview copy (video-preview.html:331-337,366-372): generic, identical for buyer/receiver, below the share divider - a code fact consistent with H3 but not decisive over H1b. preview_opened=28-34/window is real, recurring traffic - weakens H4.
diagnosis.what_the_evidence_supports: The evidence firmly supports only: (a) real recurring preview traffic (H4 contradicted), and (b) arrivers engage the preview PAGE and do load it (H1a, the coarse 'never open the video' reach failure, contradicted). It does NOT establish that arrivers scrolled past the video + Send CTA + divider to READ the below-fold review ask. Consequently H3 (generic seller-oriented copy is seen and fails to motivate) and H1b (the ask is never scrolled into view below the fold) are NOT distinguished by this evidence - both produce the observed ~0. H3 is the code-fact-plausible cause I am betting on, but it is a bet, not an established fact.
diagnosis.what_it_cannot_distinguish: Two competing ~0-producing causes remain unresolved. (1) H1b - below-fold visibility: I have no scroll-depth data, so I cannot show the review section (below the autoplay video, the Send CTA, and an <hr> divider) was ever rendered on-screen; the low active-seconds sessions (7s) are consistent with never reaching it. (2) H2 - redundancy: I cannot link 'clicked review in-app' to the same person's later 'opened preview' at this N, and the ~61% in-app non-click rate that would bound it is itself lag-truncated and overstated, so it caps EV only weakly. Because H1b and H2 cannot be ruled out, the fix is justified NOT as a proven copy problem but as an asymmetric, reversible bet on a currently-dead (~0) surface where downside is bounded at ~0 - see cause_verification.why_for_wins.

plan.title: Delight-anchored, honest review ask on the video-preview page (copy on pre- AND post-share states) + a nearly-free ride-along review-section-viewed instrument
plan.targets: Review ask on the video-preview page: video_started -> review click via source=video_preview_buyer / video_preview_receiver (leak #3). Plus a diagnostic side-goal: fire a one-time review_section_viewed event so a FUTURE cycle can separate H1b (ask never scrolled into view) from H3 (seen, ignored) on this dead surface.
plan.mechanism: A review is unpaid effort a user gives for emotional reasons - pride in what they made and gratitude. Right now the preview ask ('Made You Smile? We would really appreciate a quick review') is generic and seller-oriented and lands while the user's task is 'send it', so it does not activate that pride at the exact moment they have just watched the finished video. TWO changes, both scoped to video-preview.html: (A) VISIBLE EXPERIMENT (copy-only, same place, below the share button): reword the ask to anchor on the just-watched creation and their pride in it, and to explicitly invite an HONEST review (Amazon-TOS aligned). CRITICALLY this rewrite is applied in THREE spots so it is consistent across pre- AND post-share states: renderBuyerPreview (video-preview.html:331-337), renderReceiverPreview (366-372), AND the post-share override in highlightReviewAsk (441), which currently overwrites the heading to '🎉 Sent! Made you smile?' - without touching that override, everyone who shares before scrolling would see the OLD generic post-share text instead of the new pride/honest copy, so half the ~28/fortnight target audience would miss the experiment. (B) RIDE-ALONG INSTRUMENT (nearly free, separate from the copy bet): attach an IntersectionObserver to the existing .review-section that fires logFunnel('review_section_viewed', {source: 'video_preview_buyer'|'video_preview_receiver'}) exactly ONCE the first time that section scrolls into the viewport, on both renders. logFunnel (video-preview.html:271) and the .review-section handle (querySelector at 437) already exist, so this is a few lines and adds no user-facing change. It gives a future cycle the read that resolves H1b vs H3: if review_section_viewed fires for many preview arrivers but review_clicked stays ~0, the ask is SEEN and the copy is what fails (H3); if review_section_viewed itself stays ~0, arrivers never scroll it into view (H1b) and copy was never the lever. This is exactly the owner-permitted 'measurement rides along with a visible change'. Combined mechanism: convert a generic post-hoc request into a delight-anchored one delivered at the peak-delight moment (pre- and post-share), and instrument the surface so the dead step can finally be diagnosed instead of absorbing ship after ship. PROPOSED COPY (design-bar compliant per FUNNEL_CONTEXT: premium/refined, sparse emoji, warm-not-pushy, and Amazon-TOS 'honest review' wording) - final strings to be settled at build: heading (pre-share) 'Proud of the video you just made?'; body 'If it brought a smile, a quick honest review helps other gift-givers find us.'; button 'Leave an honest review'; post-share heading (highlightReviewAsk) 'Sent! Proud of what you made?' with the same body. This drops the current stacked ⭐/❤️ emoji down to at most a single subtle mark, keeps the tone warm rather than the current seller-oriented 'we would really appreciate', and explicitly contains 'honest review' (the current copy does not), fixing the TOS gap the audit flagged.
plan.assumed_cause: BET (not established fact): H3 - the preview review ask may convert ~0 because it is generic and seller-oriented and does not connect to the delight of the video just watched. The evidence rules out the coarse reach failure (people do load and engage the page) but CANNOT rule out H1b (the ask is below the share divider and never scrolled into view) or H2 (redundancy) - each of which produces the same ~0. I am acting on H3 because it is the only one addressable by a zero-downside copy-only edit; I am NOT claiming it is proven. I also do NOT move the ask above the share CTA (a reshuffle that would compete with the share the business needs).

cause_verification.for: Code fact (video-preview.html:331-337 buyer, 366-372 receiver): the ask is generic, identical for both roles, references nothing about the video just watched, and sits below the share divider whose CTA is 'Send My Gift Message'/'Send My Thank You'. PostHog session_recordings (6 in-window preview sessions) show people DO load and engage the PAGE without clicking review (07-21 16:14 active=45s clicks=13 keys=0; 07-21 14:21 active=7s clicks=6; 07-20 02:59 active=7s clicks=6). IMPORTANT LIMIT: this establishes only page engagement, NOT that anyone scrolled past the video + Send CTA + divider to see the below-fold review section - I have no scroll-depth data, and the 7s-active sessions are consistent with never reaching it. So I CANNOT assert 'seen and ignored'; H3 (generic copy fails to motivate) is a plausible-by-code-fact bet, not an evidenced fact, and is not distinguished from H1b (never scrolled into view).
cause_verification.against: The two competing causes that would kill this fix are H2 REDUNDANCY (they already declined the in-app ask minutes earlier) and H1b BELOW-FOLD (the ask is never scrolled into view). On H2 I looked at in-app video_started->review_clicked = 39.3% (11/28), i.e. ~61% of video-makers did not click in-app - BUT this is a lag-truncated same-window ratio (FUNNEL_CHANGELOG: review clicks lag video creation by days), so it OVERSTATES the un-converted audience and is only a loose upper bound, not proof of a large second-chance pool. On H1b I have NO scroll-depth data and cannot show the below-divider section was ever on-screen. I also could NOT link 'clicked review in-app' to the same person's later preview open at this N. Net: neither H2 nor H1b can be eliminated; both remain real, unresolved caps on EV. I am not claiming to have refuted them.
cause_verification.why_for_wins: The cause is NOT settled at ship time (H1b below-fold and H2 redundancy both survive and both produce the same ~0), so the COPY change is justified as an asymmetric, reversible bet - not on any 'seen-and-ignored' fact. Basis: the surface yields ~0 today, the copy edit stays inside the existing review-section (share CTA and layout untouched) and is fully reversible, so downside is bounded at ~0 while upside is open; it also brings the ask into explicit 'honest review' TOS alignment regardless of conversion. WHAT CHANGED vs the audited version: the ride-along review_section_viewed instrument means this ship is no longer permanently un-gradeable. GRADING RULE (binding on future cycles), now CONDITIONAL on the instrument: a persistent ~0 preview review-click is only an UNINFORMATIVE null while H1b cannot be excluded. Once the review_section_viewed event has accumulated enough events (a future cycle), the ambiguity resolves: (i) if review_section_viewed fires for a substantial share of preview arrivers yet review_clicked stays ~0, H1b is excluded and a continued ~0 CAN legitimately be graded as 'this copy, when seen, does not motivate preview reviews' (H3) - a real, reportable read; (ii) if review_section_viewed itself stays ~0, H1b is confirmed - the ask is never scrolled into view, copy was never the lever, and the next cycle should attack visibility/placement, not copy. Until that instrument read exists, a bare ~0 on review clicks still MUST NOT be read as 'delight-copy does not work' and must not be used to retire the review-copy mechanism. And no verdict of worked/worse on the copy may be claimed unless tools/significance.mjs prints SIGNIFICANT.

plan.why_the_rate_is_what_it_is: Converters here give unpaid effort (writing an Amazon review) in exchange for the emotional payoff of pride/gratitude - there is no material reward, and offering one would violate Amazon TOS. At the preview moment the user's goal is to SEND the video to the recipient; the review ask is a secondary, generic request competing with that goal, so it only lands for the small subset already moved by pride. Anchoring the copy on the video they just made is an attempt to raise that pride signal at the moment it is highest.
what_would_have_to_be_true: A meaningful share of preview arrivers have NOT already clicked review on the in-app screen (WEAKLY supported: the ~61% in-app non-click figure is lag-truncated and overstated, so it is a loose upper bound on the un-converted second-chance pool, not a firm floor).

Preview arrivers actually scroll to and read the below-divider review ask (UNVERIFIED TODAY, but the ride-along review_section_viewed instrument is designed to answer exactly this in a future cycle: if the event fires the ask is seen, if it stays ~0 it is not (H1b) and copy cannot help).
Delight/pride-anchored, honest copy raises review intent more than the current generic seller-oriented copy at this moment (unproven - the bet).

The reworded copy actually reaches BOTH pre-share and post-share viewers (SECURED by this revision: the rewrite is applied to renderBuyerPreview, renderReceiverPreview, AND the highlightReviewAsk post-share override at line 441, so sharers no longer fall back to the old generic heading).
The change does not weaken the primary share CTA (guaranteed: copy-only edit inside the existing review-section, below share; the share button is untouched).
plan.second_order_effects: The primary CTA on preview is SHARE, which drives the recipient loop (video.html -> potentially more videos/reviews); the review ask must stay subordinate to it. This change is copy-only inside the existing review-section below the share button (plus the post-share heading override), so it does not move, resize, or compete with the share CTA - share is unaffected. Editing the highlightReviewAsk override changes only the words in the same in-place card that already exists post-share (the June non-destructive pulse/scroll behaviour is preserved), so no post-share behaviour regresses. The ride-along review_section_viewed event is a single fire-once logFunnel write per preview session (same /api/track path already used by preview_opened), negligible write volume and no user-facing effect. It does not touch the in-app thank-you review ask (the current review engine, 11/11 clicks) or the Klaviyo email-redirect path (review clicks via phase=email_redirect: 0 this window, 2 prior), so those review sources are unchanged. One step further: bringing the word 'honest' into the on-page ask keeps us squarely inside Amazon TOS and consistent across pre-share and post-share states.
plan.strongest_case_against: A sceptic who knows this business would say: 'Preview review clicks are ~0 because these users already saw and declined the in-app review ask minutes earlier - the moment is spent, and the surface was already attacked once in June and stayed dead. You are polishing a corpse and spending your one visible ship on a surface that structurally cannot convert, AND you cannot even learn from it.' My honest answer concedes part of this: I CANNOT prove the audience is un-converted (the ~61% in-app non-click figure is lag-truncated and overstates the second-chance pool) and I CANNOT prove today the below-divider ask is even seen (no scroll data). So I do not claim the surface 'structurally can convert'. I ship anyway because: (1) preview is a genuinely better-timed ask when it IS seen (they have now WATCHED the video, which the in-app screen never showed them); (2) the June attempt was a different mechanism (a post-share attention pulse), not a motivational copy reframe, so this is not a repeat; (3) the surface is at ~0, so a copy-only reversible edit has downside bounded at ~0 while upside is open - the asymmetric, compounding bet this job is built to make. On the 'cannot even learn' charge specifically: this revision answers it - the ride-along review_section_viewed instrument means a future cycle CAN separate H1b (never seen) from H3 (seen, ignored), so the surface stops absorbing blind ships. On grading: if review clicks do NOT move over 4-8 weeks, that is not YET a result that retires delight-copy WHILE the instrument still shows ~0 section-viewed (H1b unexcluded); but once the instrument shows the section IS widely seen and clicks are still ~0, that null becomes an informative H3 read, not an excuse. No worked/worse verdict on the copy without a SIGNIFICANT significance.mjs print.
plan.expected_effect: Two distinct expectations. (1) On the copy bet: a small, likely-unmeasurable increase in preview-sourced review clicks (source=video_preview_buyer/receiver), net-new honest reviews on top of the in-app thank-you screen. At ~28 preview opens/fortnight and a ~13-20pt significance bar, this will almost certainly read 'not yet measurable' for many cycles; the value is compounding, not a single provable win. (2) On the ride-along instrument: review_section_viewed should begin accumulating from day one, and within a few cycles give a countable answer to whether preview arrivers actually see the below-divider ask (H1b) - a diagnostic read that is available regardless of whether the copy bet ever reaches significance.

tradeoff.gained: Potentially a few net-new honest reviews per fortnight from a currently-wasted, high-delight surface (now reaching BOTH pre- and post-share viewers), with the ask brought into explicit 'honest review' TOS alignment. PLUS a durable diagnostic gain independent of the copy bet: the review_section_viewed instrument resolves whether this dead surface is a visibility (H1b) or motivation (H3) problem, so no future cycle has to guess blind here again.
tradeoff.risked: Near-nothing. The surface already produces ~0 preview-sourced review clicks (0 this window, 2 prior), so there is no working number to break. The share CTA is untouched (copy-only, below share); the highlightReviewAsk edit changes only wording in the same post-share card that already exists (pulse/scroll behaviour preserved); the review_section_viewed write is one fire-once event on the existing /api/track path; and the in-app thank-you review engine (11/11 clicks this window) and the Klaviyo email-redirect review path (0 this window, 2 prior) are not modified.
unverified_assumptions: Whether the below-divider review ask is ever scrolled into view (H1b) - I have NO scroll-depth data TODAY, so at ship time this remains unverified; but the ride-along review_section_viewed instrument added in this revision is designed to answer it within a few cycles, converting this from a permanent unknown into a measurable read.

Whether preview arrivers are disproportionately people who already clicked review in-app (redundancy, H2) - cannot be linked per-person at this N; only weakly bounded by the ~61% in-app non-click rate, which is itself lag-truncated and overstates the un-converted pool.
